title: Cap. VI Arg. 11: that doctrine empties election of efficacy toward the elect in the way
latin: Illa doctrina non recte explicat praedestinationem sive electionem, quae fructum, nullam efficaciam electionis agnoscit quoad electos in via salutis dirigendos, conservandos, atque ad ipsam metam eandem perducendos. Nam sacrae Scripturae specialem quandam operationem et providentiam Dei denotant a decreto electionis manantem, quae electos ab omnibus iis malis liberat, quae illorum salutem alioquin impedirent.
pass_a: That doctrine does not rightly explain predestination or election, which acknowledges the fruit, no efficacy of election as regards the elect to be directed in the way of salvation, to be conserved, and to be led through to the same goal itself. For the sacred Scriptures denote a certain special operation and providence of God flowing from the decree of election, which frees the elect from all those evils which would otherwise impede their salvation.
pass_b: That doctrine does not rightly explain predestination or election: it grants the fruit, but no efficacy of election toward directing, keeping, and bringing the elect through to the goal on the way of salvation. Holy Scripture marks a special operation and providence of God flowing from the election decree — freeing the elect from all those evils that would otherwise block their salvation.

lemmas.gloss: no efficacy of election toward the elect in the way
special providence flowing from the election decree

title: Cap. VI Arg. 11: Matt. 24 — for the elect days shortened; God removes every obstacle
latin: Horsum spectant illa Christi Servatoris dicta, Matt. xxiv: Ita ut in errorem inducantur, si fieri posset, etiam electi. Propter electos breviabuntur dies illi. Tale est ergo decretum electionis, ut ratione illius Deus in se suscipiat omnes obices removere, quae salutem electorum impedirent, et iis ea media procurare, quae salutem eorundem infallibiliter producent.
pass_a: Hither look those sayings of Christ the Savior, Matt. 24: So that into error may be led, if it were possible, even the elect. For the elect's sake those days shall be shortened. Such therefore is the decree of election, that by reason of it God takes upon himself to remove all obstacles which would impede the salvation of the elect, and to procure for them those means which will infallibly produce their salvation.
pass_b: So Christ's words in Matt. 24: to lead astray, if possible, even the elect — and for the elect's sake those days will be shortened. The election decree is of that kind: by it God takes on himself to remove every obstacle that would block the elect's salvation, and to procure means that will infallibly produce it.

lemmas.gloss: elect not finally deceived; days shortened for them
God removes all obstacles to elect salvation

title: Cap. VI Arg. 11: Rom. 8:28 — all things work for good for the predestined and called
latin: Huc etiam tendit illud Apostoli, Rom. viii. 28: Omnia in bonum eorum cooperantur, qui praedestinati sunt, et secundum propositum vocati. Speciali nimirum Dei providentia ita res omnes dirigente, ut quae maxime infesta videantur illorum saluti, eandem nihilo minus promoveant.
pass_a: Hither also tends that of the Apostle, Rom. 8:28: All things work together for good for those who are predestinated, and called according to purpose. Namely by the special providence of God so directing all things, that those which seem most hostile to their salvation nonetheless promote the same.
pass_b: So also Paul, Rom. 8:28: all things work together for good for those who are predestined and called according to purpose — God's special providence so steering all things that what looks most hostile to their salvation still advances it.

lemmas.gloss: all things cooperate for good for the predestined
special providence directing even hostile things

title: Cap. VI Arg. 11: Arminian foresight election — no operative force left for the way
latin: Jam e contra pensitemus hanc, quam fingunt Arminiani, electionem, ex antecedanea fidei perseverantis praevisione. Talis electio tollit omnem vim operatricem electionis, quoad electos in via salutis conservandos aut promovendos. Nam qui ad vitam non eliguntur, nisi ex intuitu praecedentis perseverantiae ad extremum usque halitum praestitae, illis electio nihil contulit ad hunc cursum in fide et sanctitate consummandum. Omnes siquidem difficultates superasse intelliguntur, atque ad ipsum limen caeli appulisse, priusquam a Deo ad vitam sive regnum caeleste praedestinentur. Omnes autem salvandos perrexisse in via fidei et sanctitatis, recta ad regnum caelorum tetendisse, et tantum non intra portas penetrasse, priusquam a Deo ad vitam praedestinati fuerint, aut virtute praedestinationis suae ullam specialem gratiam a Deo acceperint, horrendum plane est, et Christianis auribus intolerandum, quae libenter admittunt illud Apostoli: Quos praedestinavit, hos et vocavit; quos vocavit, hos et justificavit; quos justificavit, hos et glorificavit, Rom. viii. 30.
pass_a: Now on the contrary let us weigh this election which the Arminians invent, from the antecedent foresight of persevering faith. Such election takes away all operative force of election, as regards the elect to be conserved or promoted in the way of salvation. For those who are not elected to life except from the intuition of preceding perseverance performed unto the last breath, to them election conferred nothing toward finishing this course in faith and holiness. For they are understood to have overcome all difficulties, and to have arrived at the very threshold of heaven, before they are predestinated by God to life or the heavenly kingdom. But that all the saved went on in the way of faith and holiness, stretched straight to the kingdom of heaven, and all but penetrated within the gates, before they were predestinated by God to life, or by virtue of their predestination received any special grace from God, is plainly horrendous, and intolerable to Christian ears, which gladly admit that of the Apostle: Whom he predestinated, these he also called; whom he called, these he also justified; whom he justified, these he also glorified, Rom. 8:30.
pass_b: Weigh by contrast the Arminian invention — election from prior foresight of persevering faith. That sort of election strips election of all operative force for keeping or advancing the elect on the way of salvation. If they are elected to life only by regard to perseverance already kept to the last breath, election gave them nothing toward finishing the course in faith and holiness. They are taken to have overcome every difficulty and reached heaven's very threshold before God predestines them to life. That all the saved pressed on in faith and holiness, aimed straight at the kingdom, and all but entered the gates before they were predestined — or received any special grace by virtue of predestination — is plainly horrendous, intolerable to Christian ears that gladly hear Paul: whom he predestined, he also called; whom he called, he also justified; whom he justified, he also glorified (Rom. 8:30).

lemmas.gloss: golden chain: predestined, called, justified, glorified

title: Cap. VI Arg. 11 close: Arminian order is Postdestinatio, not Praedestinatio
latin: Si nullum aliud argumentum suppeteret nobis, hoc unicum abunde infringere et evertere posset illam praedestinationem Arminianam, quod homines ponat tum demum ad vitam aeternam praedestinari, cum ad ipsam, superatis omnibus difficultatibus et periculis, pervenerint: quae rectius Postdestinatio quam Praedestinatio dicatur.
pass_a: If no other argument were at hand for us, this one alone could abundantly break and overturn that Arminian predestination, that it sets men down as predestinated to eternal life only then, when they have arrived at it itself, all difficulties and dangers having been overcome: which may more rightly be called Postdestination than Predestination.
pass_b: Even if we had no other argument, this alone would amply shatter that Arminian predestination: it has men predestined to eternal life only once they have already arrived, every difficulty and danger overcome. That is more rightly called Postdestination than Predestination.
